[CONSOLIDATED HISTORY] Russia‑Turkey Black‑Sea DMZ (1901‑1902) was initially respected, keeping SEV, ANK, CON and SMY off‑limits. Turkey broke it in Fall 1902 by moving A ARM → SEV with fleet support, dislodging Russia’s fleet and ending the DMZ. Since then Turkey has been unreliable and refuses any new DMZ. Austria‑Russia non‑aggression pact (1901) collapsed when Austria moved A GAL → RUM with two supports, forcing a bounce against Russia’s F SEV → RUM. Austria remains hostile, repeatedly threatening the Balkans and refusing to leave RUM open. No further cooperation can be expected. Germany has become openly hostile. In Spring 1903 Germany warned against any Russian move into UKR and then advanced A UKR → MOS, bouncing Russia’s A MOS and signalling a direct attack on Russia’s sole supply centre. Germany also rejected any Black‑Sea DMZ and offers no support. Italy has been friendly but unable to provide naval assistance. It supports a Black‑Sea DMZ in principle but cannot convoy fleets this turn and has focused on its own conflict with France. France is a reliable diplomatic ally. It has repeatedly affirmed the DMZ proposal and offered alliance support, though it has not provided convoys or direct military aid yet. France remains open to cooperation against Germany and Austria. England has only offered a general non‑aggression pact and refused a convoy to St. Petersburg. No further diplomatic leverage. Current strategic position (Fall 1903): - Supply centres: MOS (only Russian centre left) and STP/SC (fleet location). - Units: A LVN (moved to MOS to hold), F STP/SC (hold), no fleet in Black Sea, SEV empty. - Threats: German A UKR targeting MOS; Austria likely to press RUM; Turkey unpredictable; no convoy path to RUM. Key priorities: 1. Regain a Black‑Sea fleet (capture SEV or secure an English convoy). 2. Secure RUM quickly, preferably with Italian or French convoy/support before Austria consolidates. 3. Defend MOS against Germany (seek support from France or Italy, or consider a retreat to LVN if necessary). 4. Re‑establish a Black‑Sea DMZ with Turkey only if they can be coerced, otherwise treat Turkey as hostile. [S1904M] Russia accepted Turkey's proposal to support Turkey's army move A SEV→MOS. Russia will support with A LVN S A SEV-MOS, giving Turkey a strength‑2 attack on MOS. No other powers offered concrete assistance; France offered diplomatic support only, Italy declined convoy requests, England cannot help, and Germany rejected any cooperation and remains hostile. Intent: Support Turkey's move A SEV→MOS with A LVN S A SEV-MOS (no other orders this turn). [S1904M] Turkey’s promise to push its army from SEV into MOS collapsed – both the SEV‑>MOS move and the supporting BLA‑>SEV fleet bounced, leaving MOS undefended and our lone LVN unit idle. Germany kept its word, bouncing our A MOS attempt and maintaining pressure on the only Russian centre. Austria honoured its aggressive stance, advancing GAL‑>UKR and supporting RUM‑>UKR, confirming they will not ease Balkan pressure. final_goals: Secure RUM as soon as possible, preferably via convoy or strong support.
Re‑establish a Black Sea presence by rebuilding a fleet in SEV once a DMZ can be restored or after securing MOS.
Defend the Russian heartland by trading MOS for Warsaw and building a stronger position in the north.
Maintain and expand diplomatic ties with France and Italy while keeping Germany and Austria isolated.
Reach 18 supply centres for world domination, adjusting strategy as the board evolves.
